summary: Tenant priority skew causes continuous-batcher co-flush amplification -> sporadic p99 spikes and 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbusAI reports intermittent p95/p99 latency elevations and periodic 504 timeouts. Problem appears correlated with mixed-size request patterns where many short-inference requests from high-priority tenants are merged with a small number of long-sequence requests from lower-priority tenants.

Impact:
- NimbusAI observed p99 latency jump from baseline ~650ms to bursts >4.8s, and sporadic 504s during 15-30 minute windows several times per day.
- Customer reports user-facing errors for synchronous requests and increased retry traffic.
- Affects their primary model endpoints serving chat completions (mpt-30b) in prod-us-west; some spillover into us-east when routing fallback occurs.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) for NimbusAI; autoscaling enabled with burst capacity off.
- Redwood serving-runtime v2026.02.14, continuous-batcher v1.12.3, scheduler v0.9.7.
- Traffic pattern: 80% short sequences (<=32 tokens) tagged high-priority, 20% long sequences (>=1024 tokens) tagged low-priority.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Run synthetic workload: 800 rps of short requests (<=32 tokens) from tenant A (priority high) and 50 rps long requests (>=1024 tokens) from tenant B (priority low) against same endpoint.
2) Enable continuous-batcher default tenant-weighting and default linger thresholds.
3) After ~10-20 minutes, observe occasional flush delays and co-flushes where small requests wait for long-request KV prep, leading to p95/p99 spikes.

Observed behavior / Logs / Metrics:
- batcher/flush_latency p95 baseline ~20ms, spikes to 1.2s; batcher/flush_latency p99 spikes to 4.8s correlated with increase in batch size variance.
- gpu-utilization saw short periods of 98% during co-flush windows; scheduler logs show a sudden serializing of a long-request with many small ones.
- api-gateway measured increased connection resets and 504s; token-level cost for affected requests increased due to retries.
- Sample log snippet (redacted):
  [2026-03-10T16:12:04Z] batcher: merged 137 requests (tenant mix: 86% short/high-priority, 14% long/low-priority), flush delayed by 720ms awaiting KV cache warm-up for long sequences

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis: tenant-priority weighting plus continuous-batcher merging policy yields priority inversion when a small number of long-sequence, low-priority requests are present; warm-up of KV/cache and attention kernel selection for long sequences stalls the coalesced execution path, amplifying latency for many short requests in the same batch.
- Verified correlation by replaying traffic with tenant-priority disabled: p99 spikes disappeared in controlled test cluster.
- Observed that batcher heuristics treat high variance in sequence length as a single batchable unit; the scheduler places merged batches on same GPU worker, causing warm-up and memory pressure.
- Related config discovered in customer profile: tenant-weighting has slight bias to prefer preserving short-request priority but not strict isolation. This allows cross-tenant merging when queue depth is high.
- Existing fail-safes (max-batch-tokens, flush-timeout) are set to conservative defaults which in this workload cause delayed flushes instead of earlier breakouts.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support temporarily enabled tenant isolation flag (per-tenant batching) for NimbusAI to force separate batch queues for long-running workloads; customer traffic showed immediate reduction in p99 spikes.
- Increased flush-timeout and lowered max-batch-tokens for the mixed endpoint as an emergency measure to reduce co-flush sizes.

Next steps / Action items:
- Engineering (batcher team) to create a targeted change: add a sequence-length-aware batch-breaker that prioritizes short-high-priority requests to avoid co-waiting for long-KV warmups (owner: @Carlos Mendes).
- Scheduler team to add per-batch preflight check to avoid scheduling heterogeneous batches on same GPU if warm-up cost exceeds threshold.
- Create an automated regression test simulating tenant-priority skew in CI load harness.
- Roll out a pilot config change to a subset of dedicated customers to validate behavior before global rollout.

Customer communication:
- Notified NimbusAI on 2026-03-10 18:00 UTC that we identified an unsafe merge pattern and applied tenant isolation as a temporary mitigation. Asked customer to monitor and report any residual errors.

Status summary:
- Root cause hypothesis validated in test cluster; short-term mitigation applied and reduced customer impact. Work remains to implement robust sequence-length-aware batching heuristics and scheduler protections.
comments: 2026-03-10 18:05 - Support (Alex Nguyen): Acknowledged issue with NimbusAI, escalated to batcher and scheduler teams. Customer-facing message sent summarizing immediate mitigation.
2026-03-10 20:30 - SRE (Carlos Mendes): Replayed production-like mix in staging. Reproduced p99 spikes when tenant-weighting allowed cross-tenant merging. Will prototype sequence-length breaker.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Customer (Nora Li, NimbusAI): Confirmed that enabling tenant isolation reduced visible 504s and p99 spikes; however latency for some long requests increased as expected. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.
2026-03-11 14:40 - Scheduler Eng (Maya Thompson): Adding preflight scheduling check to avoid mixing large-seq jobs. Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/realtime-batcher/pull/512

investigation_notes: Controlled replay validated that disabling cross-tenant merging prevents p99 spikes. Instrumented KV warm-up path shows 400-800ms additional latency when long sequences enter an otherwise short-request batch. Priority inversion occurs because batcher merging aggregates on queue age and not on variance of token lengths. Tracker created for sequence-length-aware breaker (internal INT-4382).
resolution: Temporary tenant isolation enabled for NimbusAI which mitigated customer-visible p99 spikes and 504s. Engineering work planned to implement sequence-length-aware batch-breaker and scheduler preflight checks. No permanent code change deployed yet.
resolution_notes: Mitigation validated in staging and applied to customer prod. Follow-up tasks tracked in INT-4382 and PR #512. Post-implementation monitoring plan to verify p95/p99 stability over 72h window after rollout.
